subjects.subject: authoring-block-vocabulary
subjects.evidence: src/components/guide/guide-markdown/parseCustomBlock.tsx:20-38 is a textbook closed-directive-set: one dispatch over an enumerated block-type list, `return null` for anything else, and parseBlocks.tsx:133-135 only emits when non-null; each block type gets its own tiny line grammar (parseCustomBlock.tsx:40-196) and Callout.tsx:16-56 enum-guards its label styling with a named fallback (`?? CALLOUT_STYLES.info`) — but the 13-locale corpus under src/data/guide/locales/ (getLocalized.ts:1-120) has no structural-equivalence check comparing translated block structure against the English source; a translator could break a directive/separator and nothing would catch it before publish (currently low-risk since the locale switcher is dormant per getLocalized.ts:6-8).

subjects.subject: hitl-approval
subjects.evidence: src/app/legal/LegalContent.tsx and src/app/legal/policies/*.tsx render static legal prose with a localStorage-backed "last seen" changelog badge (src/data/policy-changelog.ts:45-61) — no autonomous action, consent flow, or review gate exists on this page (grepped for consent/accept/reject/approve/escalate: only "Acceptance of Terms" prose text). hitl-approval's precondition (an action boundary needing human judgment) fails entirely; this is documentation, not an agent action surface.

subjects.subject: client-state
subjects.evidence: src/lib/server/json-file-store.ts:1, src/lib/fileLock.ts, and src/lib/server/rate-limit.ts:31 all declare `import "server-only"` — this is Node-side file-backed persistence, an in-process write lock, and an in-memory rate limiter running in Next.js route handlers, never a browser. client-state's precondition (a long-lived client application's state) does not hold here at all; this looks like a lexical mismatch (the matcher likely keyed on "state"/"persistence" vocabulary) rather than a real governance relationship — flagged as a coverage question in the report, not judged as a deviation.

subjects.subject: templates-scaffolding
subjects.evidence: src/lib/templates.ts:18-32 defines AgentTemplate as static hardcoded metadata + a fixed YAML `config` string with no parameter/dimension model; src/app/templates/[id]/TemplateDetail.tsx:63-102 offers only copy-to-clipboard and a `personas://` deep link that hands off adoption to a separate desktop app. This repo owns browse+preview only — the interview, adoption transaction, readiness-prerequisites check, integrity manifest, and portability rewriting that templates-scaffolding governs have no home here; they belong (if they exist) to the desktop app this page links out to.

subjects.subject: knowledge-registry
subjects.evidence: src/app/dashboard/knowledge/MemoriesView.tsx and KnowledgeDenseTable.tsx display per-persona runtime learned patterns (KnowledgePattern: successCount/failureCount/confidence/avgCostUsd) and memory-conflict resolution for one agent fleet — this is agent runtime memory, not a shared, multi-consumer repository with lanes, a write path, or a catalog-as-sync-key. knowledge-registry's precondition (an organizational registry consumed by many codebases and tools) does not hold; likely a lexical match on "knowledge" rather than a real governance relationship — flagged as a coverage question.

subjects.subject: hitl-approval
subjects.evidence: Real, not mock: api.ts:355-361 uses mockApi only when isDemo. The escalate rung writes client state only; setEscalationEnabled and reviewUtils have zero call sites.

subjects.subject: cost-metering
subjects.evidence: src/app/dashboard/observability/activity-view/AthenaSpendLane.tsx:47-105 and PerformanceView.tsx:63/103-110 (BUDGET_THRESHOLD banner) only render spend figures sourced from mock fixtures (useActivityMetrics.ts:26 via mockApi) or api.getObservability — no price table, usage ledger, preflight estimation, or budget-enforcement gate exists anywhere in these files; the 0.8 threshold banner is a presentational comparison, not an enforcement point that blocks a call.

subjects.subject: hitl-approval
subjects.evidence: src/app/dashboard/observability/performance-view/PerformanceHealthPanel.tsx:15-104 and PerformanceHealthIssueRow.tsx render health-issue status (open/auto_fixed/resolved) read-only, with no approve/reject/consent affordance anywhere in this context's files — hitl-approval's precondition (an action boundary where a person must pause a machine before it acts) does not hold; this is a post-hoc display surface, not an action surface. Contrast the sibling Agent Operations Dashboard/Manual Review Queue, which does own a real (if incomplete) approve/reject flow.

subjects.subject: delivery-guarantees
subjects.evidence: Retry publishes a NEW event (eventStore.ts:170-177); the original stays failed, so each click adds a duplicate and the dead-letter lane never drains.

subjects.subject: client-state
subjects.evidence: src/lib/clearUserCaches.ts:38 correctly wires eventStore.reset() into identity-scoped-eviction (clears both the in-memory buffer and the persisted retryCounts on every identity flip), and src/stores/eventStore.ts:104-141 plus src/hooks/useEventStream.ts:100-153 realize solid async-race-guards (dedup-by-id, merge-not-replace refetch, single-EventSource guard) and status-fsms (connectionStatus enum) — but eventStore.ts:26-52 persists replay retryCounts to localStorage with no version stamp, violating persistence-and-migration's versioned-contract rule.

subjects.subject: fleet-orchestration
subjects.evidence: src/app/dashboard/home/home-page/FleetSessionsStrip.tsx:8-31 renders MOCK_FLEET_SESSIONS, a static fixture array with no registry/lifecycle/dispatch machinery behind it, and is gated behind isDemo at the call site (src/app/dashboard/home/page.tsx:172-181, comment: "Pure fixtures with no synced source") — never shown to real users. fleet-orchestration's precondition (a real orchestrated multi-session fleet) does not hold in this repo; presentation is honestly disclosed as demo-only.
